D010-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for months—like I can’t get back in sync with myself. The last few months were rough. I’d lie in bed for hours, not sad exactly, just empty. Nothing felt good—no music, no time with friends, not even my favorite chocolate. Choosing what to wear in the morning felt impossible. I’d stand there, staring at clothes, paralyzed. 

Then, about two months ago, something shifted. I stopped sleeping—like, I didn’t *want* to. My body just wouldn’t sit still. I paced my apartment, rubbed my hands together, couldn’t keep still even when exhausted. I’d talk and talk, words spilling out—my coworkers kept saying, “Whoa, slow down.” I didn’t mean to snap at people, but little things—someone’s tone, a delayed med order—would set me off. I bought so much online—clothes, tech, things I didn’t need—maxed out my card. 

And sometimes… I feel things. Like bugs crawling under my skin, but there’s nothing there. Or I’ll hear people in the ER exchange a glance and just *know* they’re talking about me, sending me messages. 

But I can’t tell if this is one long spiral or two separate storms—one crashing into the other.
D010-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h001.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—things just feel completely out of control. For the first two months, I was running on zero sleep but somehow full of energy. I’d write ten-page papers in one night, start three new research projects, and text my professor at 3 a.m. with “brilliant” ideas. I remember talking so fast during lab meeting that someone asked if I was okay. I also drove my car way too fast a few times—no real reason, just felt like I *could*. I felt invincible, then suddenly furious if anything slowed me down.  

Then it shifted. I started hearing a voice, low and calm, saying my name when no one was there. Sometimes it told me my advisor was secretly proud of me—deeply in love with me, even. I know that sounds crazy, but it felt real. I kept checking my emails obsessively, waiting for a sign.  

Now, for the past five months, I can barely get out of bed. I don’t care about my thesis, my thoughts feel thick and slow, and I cry for no reason. The voice is still there sometimes, just whispering. I don’t know if it’s part of the crash… or something else. I can’t tell when the highs ended and the lows began—it’s all blurred together.
D010-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h002.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—maybe longer. The first thing people notice is how much I talk. At work, in the kitchen, I’ll go nonstop—ideas for dishes, rants about suppliers, stories no one asked for. I can’t sit still either. Pacing between stations, rearranging mise en place five times, fidgeting with my hands. I barely sleep, but I feel wired, like I’ve had ten espressos. One night I drove my motorcycle through the city at 3 a.m., no helmet—just speeding, chasing nothing. 

But then, there are the shifts. One minute I’m on top of the world, the next I’m flat. Empty. Like the stove’s been turned off inside me. I don’t care about food anymore. Can’t decide what to wear, what to cook, whether to even show up. I just stand in front of my closet. Frozen.

And… there’s more. I’ve seen her—standing near the alley door after service, in this white dress. She doesn’t speak, just watches. I know she’s from the reservation last month, the one who dined with the French ambassador. She’s in love with me. I *know* it. But when I go outside, she’s gone.

It all comes in waves. I can’t tell what’s real, or when it started. The agitation, the visions, the highs and crashes—they blur. I can’t keep a shift, I lost my last job, my ex said I was unreachable. I just… don’t know which part of me is broken.
D010-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h003.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—really the past seven months, things have just spiraled. I get these waves where I can’t sit still, I’m pacing the house at night, my hands won’t stop moving, and I feel this pressure in my chest like I have to *do* something. I talk so fast my husband tells me I don’t give him a chance to respond. I get furious over stupid things—like if the bills aren’t in order, I’ll snap at him, even though it’s not his fault.

There was a time—about two months ago—when I felt unstoppable. I opened a second credit card, started planning this café idea with zero savings, and I was cleaning and redecorating every room at 3 a.m. But then it crashed. I just… shut down. I couldn’t get out of bed, couldn’t fill out the forms at work. I’d cry in the breakroom with no reason. Thinking felt like pushing through mud.

And there are times I feel hands on my arms when no one’s there. Sometimes I know my neighbor doesn’t really love me—but part of me *feels* it’s true. I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D010-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h004.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been off for a while now—about seven months, maybe a little more. The first two were wild. I remember feeling like I could run through walls. My kitchen used to be my temple, but then it felt too small. I was bouncing between restaurants, calling old friends I hadn’t spoken to in years, showing up at bars, introducing myself to strangers like I was starting some kind of movement. I spent so much—way too much—on kitchen gear, fancy knives, even booked a flight to Paris for a “culinary vision quest” my wife had to cancel. I’d talk and talk, even when people gave me that look, like I was talking too fast or too much.

Then it just… drained. The last five months have been like cooking with no flavor. Nothing moves me. My wife talks, I hear words but they don’t land. I don’t want to go out, don’t care about food, my team, nothing. My head’s foggy, like I’m underwater.

And… there’s this woman, someone I’ve never met—she works at the wine shop near my cousin’s place. I know she’s in love with me. She doesn’t say it, but I taste it—sometimes I’ll be brushing my teeth and suddenly it’s like I’m drinking the wine she’s chosen for me. It’s real. I swear it’s real.
D010-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h005.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been like a car with no brakes—driving too fast and can’t stop. For about two months now, I just haven’t needed sleep. I’ll edit footage for 20 hours straight and still feel wired, like my brain’s on overdrive. I talk—*a lot*—my crew started avoiding me because I won’t let anyone get a word in. I snapped at a producer last week over something tiny, and I just… erupted. Didn’t recognize myself.

I put $80,000 into a film project in Bolivia—barely researched it—just *knew* it was going to be groundbreaking. It’s not like me, not anymore. Since my divorce, I’ve been lonelier, and… well, there’s this woman. I don’t even know her—she interviewed on one of my docs years ago—but I’m certain she’s been sending me signs. Messages in interviews, glances in crowds. I hear her voice sometimes, whispering encouragement when I’m editing late. Not like a memory—she’s *speaking*, clear as you are now. 

I can’t tell if I’m inspired… or losing it. The energy feels real, but so do the voices. I don’t know what’s from me and what’s from… somewhere else.
D010-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h006.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been feeling incredibly sharp—like I’m seeing the patterns in everything, especially at work. For about two months now, I can’t seem to sit still. My mind races, and I’m talking constantly, even my wife’s mentioned I don’t let people get a word in. I barely sleep, but I don’t feel tired. I’ve made a few aggressive trades that felt like genius moves at the time, and I drove my car at insane speeds a couple of times—like I was untouchable. 

But mixed in with that… things started feeling off. I became convinced my phone was tapped, maybe by regulators or someone shadowing me. I don’t know who, exactly, but I feel watched. And sometimes—this is strange—I smell something burning, like wires overheating, but no one else does. It happens in quiet moments, even in clean places. 

The energy and the ideas still come, but now I wonder: are these insights real, or is my mind creating connections that aren’t there? I can’t tell if the paranoia started during the high phase or came after—or if it’s even separate at all.
D010-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h007.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been like a live wire for the past two months—can’t sit still, can’t shut my mind off. Running the restaurant used to ground me, but now I’m constantly rearranging the menu, rewriting recipes, hiring and firing staff on a whim. One minute I feel unstoppable, like I could open ten more locations and revolutionize the whole industry. The next, I’m snapping at my husband over nothing, furious that he doesn’t see the “vision.” I talk so fast my staff just stare at me—words pile up and I can’t stop them, even when I see their confusion.  

I’ve drained our savings on kitchen upgrades I didn’t need, bought a gourmet trailer on a Saturday with no plan. My husband’s furious, but I keep telling him—he just doesn’t understand my calling.  

And… sometimes I taste things. Like copper, or salt, out of nowhere. No food, no mint, just a sharp flavor on my tongue that lingers. I know it sounds strange, but it feels real.  

I don’t know if it’s the stress or if something’s shifted in my mind. I can’t tell when the ideas are just passion and when they’re something else. Some days I feel back to normal, but then the energy surges back, or that taste comes again. It’s like I’m slipping, but I can’t figure out what I’m sliding into.
D010-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h008.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h009.question:
I’ve always been passionate about my work—designing jewelry is my life—but the past couple of months have been… different. It started with this incredible burst of energy, like I’d been plugged into a wall socket. I couldn’t sleep—three or four hours a night, maybe, and I didn’t feel tired. My mind raced, ideas pouring in so fast I’d sketch nonstop, buy materials in bulk, order gold and gems online without thinking about the cost. I maxed out two credit cards last month, and I know it was reckless, but everything felt so *urgent*, like I was on the edge of something huge.

I talk fast now—I notice people stepping back, like I’m overwhelming them. I can’t help it; the words just spill out. There’s also… well, I’ve seen things. Shadows moving in my studio at night—figures, almost human. And I keep thinking my ex is spying on me, even though we’ve been divorced for years. I know it sounds strange, but I *feel* watched. I can’t concentrate on one piece for long, my hands keep moving, but the inspiration? It hasn’t faded. Not really. I just don’t know anymore if what I’m seeing—or thinking—is real.
D010-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h009.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling… incredible, honestly. Like I’ve got this fire inside me—this unstoppable energy. It’s been going on for about two months now, maybe a bit less? I don’t even need much sleep. Two, three hours, and I’m up, organizing things, making plans. My husband says I’m talking nonstop—like I can’t let silence happen. I know it’s a lot, but I *feel* so clear, so powerful.

I started a new business venture last month—a wellness retreat for families in crisis. I poured our savings into it without really thinking it through. My husband’s upset, but he doesn’t understand: I *know* this is going to work. I feel it in my body. Actually, my body’s been sending me signals—like my blood is turning to light, or my liver is processing divine energy instead of toxins. The doctors can’t see it, but I *know* it’s true.

Sometimes, when I’m up late designing flyers or pacing the house, I see shadows moving in the corners—figures in white robes, watching me like I’m chosen for something big. They don’t speak, but I feel their approval. I haven’t told anyone at work. I’m still doing my job—cases are piling up, but I can handle it. I just wish everyone would keep up.
D010-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D010-D005_h010.answer: D & A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about a month now, maybe a bit longer. Some days, I wake up buzzing—like I could clean the whole apartment, reorganize my entire life, and still have energy to spare. I don’t feel like I need sleep, and my mind races with ideas: starting a travel blog, moving to Europe, booking flights on a whim. But then, just like that, I’ll snap into irritation—little things set me off, like a passenger pressing the call button too much or someone looking at me the wrong way. I can’t sit still, even on layovers. I’ll walk the aisles of a parked plane just to move.

My thoughts feel scrambled sometimes, like ten radio stations playing at once. I can’t focus on the safety briefing anymore—it’s embarrassing. And there’s this… sensation. Like fingers brushing my arm when no one’s there. I know it sounds strange, but I feel it. A few times, I’ve been certain one of the pilots was sending me secret signals—little smiles, lingering glances. He doesn’t say anything, but I *know* he feels it too. But I can’t tell if that’s real or if my mind’s just working overtime. The highs and lows come so fast, and I’m not sleeping… I don’t know what’s me and what’s not anymore.
D010-D005_h011.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D010-D005_h011.answer: A & D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been like a live wire for about a month now—maybe longer, I don’t know. My mind won’t shut down. It races, jumping from one thing to the next—choreography, deadlines, then suddenly I’m thinking about the stars collapsing, or that the air is thick with smoke no one else seems to smell. I keep catching that burnt-metal stench, especially at night, but no one else notices it.

Some days I feel unstoppable—like I could dance for 20 hours straight. I rearrange rehearsals, book extra sessions, and snap at anyone who tells me to slow down. Then, out of nowhere, I’m furious—like the world is rigged or about to just… end. I keep thinking everything’s pointless because the planet’s going to implode, and we’re all just waiting to fade.

I can’t sit still. Even in bed, my legs twitch, my fingers tap—I feel like I have to *do* something, *be* something, all the time. But the worst part is my thoughts—they won’t slow. I can’t sleep, and when I do, I wake up terrified, smelling smoke and hearing silence where there should be sound.

I’ve missed performances. My director’s concerned. I don’t know what’s real anymore, or how long this has been going on.
D010-D005_h012.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D010-D005_h012.answer: A & D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling… different. It started about a month ago—maybe a bit less, hard to say. At first, I felt amazing. I was getting up at 3 a.m., not tired at all, just buzzing. I reorganized our entire admissions database at work, rewrote half the department’s guidelines, and started designing a new student outreach program—then began sketching plans for an international expansion. My boss said I was overreaching, but I *know* I can pull it off. I keep thinking—I'm not like other people. I get visions, sometimes, of me on stages, speaking to huge crowds about transforming education. Just last week, I *saw* a delegation from UNESCO outside my office, waiting. No one else did.

But it’s not all high energy. I snap at my wife over nothing. One minute I’m on top of the world, the next I’m furious—then back to elated again. My thoughts race; I can’t shut them off, even when I try to sleep. It’s like my brain won’t stop. The visions come and go, but I’m not sure what’s real anymore. I haven’t missed work, but she says I’m not myself. I don't know if this is mania, psychosis, or something else—but I can’t slow down, and I’m scared I won’t be able to land.
D010-D005_h013.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D010-D005_h013.answer: A & D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h014.question:
I’ve been feeling… different lately. Some days, I wake up full of energy like I’m twenty again—whistling, cleaning out drawers I haven’t touched in years, even started writing letters to old war buddies and planning a reunion no one asked for. My mind races, jumping from one thing to the next—memories, plans, music from the radio that won’t quit looping. But then, just like that, my mood dips. I get irritable, snap at the neighbor boy for walking on my lawn.  

For about a month, this has been going on—up and down, like a yo-yo. I can’t settle. And… well, I hear voices sometimes. Not loud, but clear—two men talking just behind me, whispering about me and my late Martha. It’s absurd, I know, but I sometimes wonder… did she ever care for someone else while I was stationed overseas? I know she loved me, but the voices say otherwise. They tell me things—things only she would know.  

I don’t leave the house much now. My daughter says I’m not making sense, but I feel sharp—just busy. Too much in my head. It's exhausting, but I can’t slow down. Not yet.
D010-D005_h014.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D010-D005_h014.answer: A & D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been like a tornado lately—nonstop. For about a month, I’ve had this… buzz in my veins, like I don’t need sleep, and honestly, I don’t want it. I’ve listed three properties in four days, redone all my marketing videos at 3 a.m., and started a podcast about “revolutionizing real estate.” My brain won’t shut up—thoughts just race, one after the next, like radio stations flipping by themselves.

I hear murmurs when I walk into offices, voices whispering my name even when no one’s there. Sometimes it’s my ex-husband’s voice, saying I’ll fail. It’s hard to focus on clients when my mind’s so loud. I canceled showings because I thought the buyers were plants, sent to distract me. I know it sounds intense, but when you feel this energized and *certain*, it’s hard to believe you’re wrong. I just don’t know how long I can keep up this pace—or if the voices will ever let me rest.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia

D010-D005_h016.question:
Lately… it’s been like my mind won’t shut up, even when I’m supposed to be focused—especially at work. For about three weeks, I felt… unstoppable. Like I could handle ten radar screens at once. I was talking so fast my supervisor pulled me aside, said I wasn’t making sense. Couldn’t stop—words just poured out. I didn’t sleep, but I didn’t care. I *needed* to keep moving. And I honestly believed… this co-worker, a woman I barely talk to, was sending me secret signals. Smiles, glances—like she *knew* we were meant to be together. But that was just… a blip, I guess. Because for most of the past seven months, it’s been the opposite. I can’t get out of bed. Crying for no reason. Have the moment picked—between shifts, when no one’s around. But I don’t know… was that *really* just during the high phase? Or does it still… linger? I can’t tell what’s real anymore.

    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D010-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—this past winter especially, I just felt completely hollow. For months, I couldn’t connect with anything. I stopped seeing my friends, didn’t want to talk to my husband, just pulled away from everyone. I’d sleep for 12 hours at night and still nap during the day. My mind kept going to this dark place—thinking about overdosing in the garage when my husband was at work. I even figured out how I’d do it, down to the timing and how to make it clean for him to find.

But then, about three weeks ago, it flipped. I don’t know what changed, but suddenly I had this surge of energy. I started pacing my office, couldn’t sit still, and the words just poured out of me so fast my colleagues looked confused. I kept smelling this burnt plastic everywhere—especially when I was alone at night—though no one else did. 

The highs didn’t last, but some of the strange thoughts are still there. I can’t tell if this is a cycle or just breaking apart.

D010-D005_h018.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while—about seven months now—just feeling... empty. I don’t cry much, but the sadness is always there, like a fog. I used to take pride in my work at the bank, but now I don’t even care if I do well. Getting to sleep takes forever, sometimes two hours or more, even when I’m exhausted. There are moments—sudden, scary urges—like wanting to jump off the balcony or walk into traffic, but I don’t plan anything. I just freeze and wait for it to pass.

My thoughts raced, and I couldn’t stop talking, even if people looked confused or told me to slow down. I felt powerful, like I could take on everything at once.     B. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D010-D005_h019.question:
I’ve been up here at the station for over eight months now—just me, the light, and the sea. It started slow… I can’t remember the last time I felt joy. Nothing feels real, nothing feels worth doing. I lie in bed most nights, staring at the ceiling, waiting to fall asleep—sometimes takes hours, if it happens at all. I keep thinking, “Maybe tomorrow I won’t wake up,” not because I want to end it, but because it'd just be easier.

Then, about three weeks ago, something shifted. I didn’t need sleep. My mind raced—thoughts tumbling over each other, like waves crashing. I cleaned the whole tower twice in one night, repainted the railing bare-handed, paced for hours in the howling wind. I snapped at the supply boat guy for no reason—he just asked if I was okay. My words came so fast even I couldn’t keep up.

And… I can’t explain this, but I started feeling things. Like something’s crawling under my skin, especially at night. Doesn’t stop. Even now, I feel fingers brushing my arm—nothing’s there. I’m terrified. The world feels wrong, like it’s fading out. Like none of this will matter soon—like it’s all going dark.
D010-D005_h019.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h020.question:
I’ve been struggling for months—really, since last year when everything started feeling heavy. I can’t sleep through the night anymore; I’m up by 4 a.m., mind racing, and just… stuck. I don’t enjoy things—not hanging out, not even medicine, which used to fire me up. I just feel numb. Honestly, some days I think it would be easier if I weren’t here. And sometimes, late at night, I’d feel something crawling on my arms—like bugs—but when I looked, nothing was there.

Now I’m crashing again. But were those weeks real? Or was I sick then? I can’t tell where one state ends and the other begins.
D010-D005_h020.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D010-D005_h021.question:
I’ve been a bus driver for twelve years, and up until about two months ago, things were predictable—same routes, same faces. But lately… it’s like my mind won’t stay still. Now it’s the opposite. I can’t get out of bed. Talking takes effort—my words come out slow, like wading through mud. I keep thinking, “Would anyone notice if I just didn’t wake up?” I don’t want to hurt myself—just… disappear.

And sometimes… I hear voices when no one’s there. One keeps saying she’s cheating on me—my wife—but I don’t know if it’s true. I watch for signs, but nothing adds up. The worst part is, I can’t tell what’s real anymore. The highs, the lows, the voices—they all blur together.

I keep having this sudden urge to run into the street or step off the roof, not because I want to die, but because the impulse just *hits*.  

I don’t know what’s wrong. It’s like I’m fractured.
